title: Explainable cohort-conditioned thresholder and rollback orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an automated rollback trigger subsystem that computes cohort-conditioned SLO thresholds (latency, error rate, token cost, throughput) and surfaces human-readable attribution for why a rollback was triggered. The system should recommend threshold adjustments using sensitivity analysis rather than fixed heuristics, support hysteresis windows and online false discovery rate control, and integrate with existing rollout/A-B/shadow traffic controllers. Goal: fewer false positives, faster diagnosis, and safer automated evacuations for model rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: The orchestrator computes per-cohort SLO baselines from historical traffic and applies a sensitivity-weighted deviation score for each metric.
Rollback decisions must include an explainability payload listing the top 3 contributing signals and their normalized impact (human-readable) in Grafana and the webhook event.
Hysteresis: must require sustained deviation for configurable window (default 3m) and support separate ramp vs steady-state thresholds.
Online FDR or Bayesian posterior fusion to control multi-metric alarm false positives is implemented and tunable per project.
Integrator compatibility: supports canary, A/B, and shadow traffic modes and exposes a stable API for the rollout controller to call (sync decision + async incident report).
Performance: decision latency for typical cohort size (<= 50 cohorts) must be < 200ms and scale linearly with cohort count.
End-to-end test coverage with synthetic backtests that include token-cost inflation scenarios and throughput spikes.
notes: 2026-03-01 - Maya created ticket: initial scope and motivation (reduce noisy auto-rollbacks for heterogeneous cohorts).
2026-03-03 - Design sync: agreed to include an explainability payload with user-facing language and a compact JSON for machine consumption (PO agreed to two levels: summary + signal breakdown).

2026-03-05 - Proposal: use normalized z-scores per metric with SHAP-style signal attribution across features (cohort, request_size, prompt_template, region). Omar proposed a hybrid approach combining bootstrap baseline intervals with posterior fusion for multi-metric aggregation.

2026-03-07 - Engineering spike: implemented prototype service that reads cohort histograms from metrics store, computes deviations, and outputs a decision score. Prototype decision latency 180ms for 20 cohorts. Memory acceptable but needs optimization for 500+ cohorts.

2026-03-08 - PM feedback (Ruth): require explicit cost-normalization for token-cost SLO so expensive long-completions don't dominate smaller prompt cohorts. Added request_size bucketing to baseline computation.

2026-03-09 - Security note: review required for webhook payloads that may include examples of customer inputs (we will scrub or hash prompt text). Filed dependency ENG-88043 for PII-scrubbing middleware.

2026-03-10 - Review feedback from Reliability (Diego): prefer configurable backoff vs immediate rollback for throughput-driven signals (e.g., throttling gateway should be first-class). Added label and dependency to coordinate with infra-rate-limiter team.
implementation_notes: Key components: (1) cohort baseline builder that consumes histogram timeseries and request metadata, (2) deviation scorer with per-metric sensitivity weights, (3) multi-metric fusion (online FDR / Bayesian fusion), (4) explainability generator that ranks contributing signals and formats summary language, (5) actuator API for canary/AB/shadow controllers. We will implement feature flags for gradual rollout and offline backtesting harness for tuning thresholds.
risks: Risk of overfitting thresholds to historical traffic; to mitigate, use holdout windows and conservative priors. Risk of latency bloat if cohort cardinality explodes; add sampling and hierarchical aggregation. Webhook payloads risk exposing prompts; ensure scrubbing/hashing middleware is in place.
next_steps: Finish prototype cleanup, add scrub middleware (ENG-88043), run 3 synthetic backtests (token-cost inflation, regional outage, mixed-cohort drift), and ship canary behind feature flag to internal prod subset.
